land.text: Herat, which Mahmud Shah and then Kamran Shah held as an independent principality from 1818

predecessors.note: HR dates the independence to 1793 ('Mahmud Shah took control of Herat, making the town and the surrounding region independent') and a revival by Firuz al-Din Mirza in 1801; Cliopatria's Durrani Empire shape keeps Herat to 1819, and the durrani-empire dossier dates the loss to 1818, which is followed.

land.text: Herat and its dependencies, conquered on 27 May 1863

successors.note: The emirate dossier records the matching gain.

capitals.name: Herat
capitals.note: HR: Herat is the capital; the coordinates are the city's.

rulers.name: Mahmud Shah
rulers.title: Shah
rulers.note: 'The first act Yar Mohammad Khan did in 1829 was to depose Mahmud Shah.'

rulers.name: Kamran Shah Durrani
rulers.title: Shah
rulers.note: Murdered in early 1842 on Yar Muhammad Khan's order.

rulers.name: Yar Muhammad Khan Alakozai
rulers.title: Vizier-i Kabir
rulers.note: Took the vizier's title, not a royal one; died 1851 (7, 11 or 29 June on the page).

rulers.name: 'Isa Khan Bardurrani
rulers.note: Surrendered Herat to Iran on 25 October 1856 and was executed.

rulers.name: Sultan Ahmad Khan
rulers.note: Installed April 1857; died 6 March 1863; his son Shah Nawaz Khan held the city to 27 May 1863.

correction.text: Herat with its dependencies: Farah (taken 1819), Badghis (a victory in 1826), the Taymani lands of Ghor and, to 1837, a hold on Sistan (HR)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row: the principality as a floor of four Natural Earth admin-1s (about 147,000 km2); HR gives no area and no frontier, only the dependencies named. Dost Mohammad's page says Farah was held by the Barakzai emirs from 30 October 1856, HR that Farah's capture in 1862 was his casus belli: Farah is kept in the shape and the conflict noted.

ledger.note: 1818: Herat becomes an independent principality under Mahmud Shah and Kamran. 'In 1818, Mahmud and later Kamran Shah took over'; the page dates Herat's first independence to 1793 ('Mahmud Shah took control of Herat') and a revival by Firuz al-Din Mirza in 1801.

region.text: Herat, besieged by the Qajar army

ledger.note: 1837: the Shah of Iran marches on Herat. 'On July 23, 1837, Mohammad Shah marched out of Tehran towards Herat'; the siege that followed lasted eight months despite Russian advisers with the Iranians. The siege's own start month is not on the page; the year is the march's.
1838: the Persian siege of Herat is lifted. 'The siege lasted eight months'; the page gives no lifting date, so the year is inferred from the length.

region.text: the Lash-Joveyn district on the Farah-Sistan side

ledger.note: 1851: under Yar Muhammad the principality extends into Lash-Joveyn. He 'expanded toward the Chahar Wilayat and Aimaq territory, and into Lash-Joveyn in 1851'. The district's earlier owners are not on the page.
1856: Iranian forces enter Herat territory. 'Iranian forces entered Herat in February 1856.'
1856: Herat falls to Iran. 'On October 25, 1856, Herat fell to the Iranian forces.'

1856: Iran occupies Herat. After the fall of 25 October 1856 'Iranian forces' held the city until the evacuation of September 1857 (Treaty of Paris, 1857: Iran forbidden to interfere in Herat's affairs 'unless necessary').
1857: Iran evacuates Herat. 'Iranian forces evacuated Herat in September 1857'; Sultan Ahmad Khan had been installed in April 1857.

region.text: Herat with its dependencies: Farah (taken 1819), Badghis (a victory in 1826), the Taymani lands of Ghor and, to 1837, a hold on Sistan (HR)

ledger.note: 1863: Dost Mohammad takes Herat. 'Ultimately they were able to capture the city on May 27, 1863, ending Herat's existence as an independent state.' DM: 'After a 10-month siege on 27 May 1863, he captured Herat.'

wars.name: Siege of Herat (1837-1838)
wars.outcome: Herat held out against the Qajar army; no border changed.
wars.note: 'On July 23, 1837, Mohammad Shah marched out of Tehran towards Herat.' The page does not name the British role.

wars.name: Persian capture of Herat
wars.outcome: Iran took Herat in October 1856 and left in September 1857 under the Treaty of Paris.
wars.note: The page does not use the name Anglo-Persian War.

wars.name: Dost Mohammad's conquest of Herat
wars.outcome: Dost Mohammad captured Herat on 27 May 1863, ending the principality.
wars.note: Farah's capture in 1862 was his casus belli (HR); the siege lasted 10 months (DM).

certainty.note: Tribal and desert frontiers with Kandahar, Sistan, Maimana and the Turkmen; no survey line until the 1857 Treaty of Paris, which names no boundary.

sources.title: Principality of Herat
sources.note: Independence 1793, revival 1801, takeover 1818, rulers, the Persian sieges of 1837-38 and 1856-57, Treaty of Paris, conquest by Dost Mohammad on 27 May 1863.

sources.title: Dost Mohammad Khan
sources.note: Herat captured on 27 May 1863 after a 10-month siege; the Farah date (30 October 1856) that conflicts with HR.

notes: Written for batch ia-03-x from two pages (budget 2-5): HR and DM. Start year: HR gives 1793 (Mahmud Shah's independence) and 1801 (Firuz al-Din Mirza's revival) before 1818; the durrani-empire dossier (ia-03-e) dates Herat's loss to 1818 and Cliopatria's Durrani shape keeps Herat to 1819, so 1818 is followed and the earlier span is a possible extension. HR says Herat was 'tributary to Qajar Iran for much of the period' without dates: no vassal pair is recorded. Disagreements: Farah (HR 1862, DM 30 October 1856). The Anglo-Persian War page was not opened (the occupation is cited to HR). Region names needed: none; the Lash-Joveyn district is read as inside the Farah admin-1.
